 Order

Dated this the 13th day of October, 2020 This criminal revision petition is directed against the judgment dated 09.11.2004 in Crl.A.No.118/2003 on the file of the Additional Sessions Court,
Thodupuzha.

The revision petitioner was the 3rd accused in S.T.No.498/2000 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Idukki and the appellant in Crl.A.No.118/2003.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The original complaint was filed by the Food Inspector, Thodupuzha Circle against A1 to A4 alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 2(ia)
(m), 7(i) and 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'the PFA Act') and the Rules framed thereunder.

3. The case of the complainant is that on 23.11.1999, he had purchased three bottles of pooja ghee from the bakery of the 1st accused situated at Vazhathopu ..3..
Grama Panchayat which is within his jurisdiction in accordance with law.
After complying with requisite formalities, three bottles of pooja ghee were sealed in the presence of the 1st accused.
Thereafter, the 1st accused produced the purchase bill to prove that he had purchased the said food item from the 2 nd accused.
A part of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis.
On 17.1.2000, the Public Analyst forwarded Form-III report through the Local Health Authority stating that the sample of ghee sent for analysis was adulterated.
The 3 rd accused is the nominee of the manufacturer.
4. During the proceedings, the 3rd accused exercised his right to get the second sample analysed through the Central Food Laboratory.
On analysis the Central Food Laboratory sent a report stating that the sample of ghee sent for analysis was adulterated as well as misbranded.
On the appearance of the accused 1 to 4 before the court, the 2nd accused filed an application to implead the 5th accused on the allegation that he had purchased the said ghee from the 5th accused.
The said application was allowed and the 5th accused was impleaded.
6. In the meanwhile, the complainant filed an application to amend the charge and incorporate Section 2 (ix)(k).
In view of the CFL report the said application was allowed and an offence of selling misbranded food article was also added to the charge.
7. During the trial, PWs.1 to 3 were examined and marked Exts.P1 to P26 on the side of the complainant.
DWs.1 and 2 were examined and marked Exts.D1 to D3 on the side of the accused.

sentences.text:
By its judgment dated 07.04.2003 the learned Magistrate found the accused 1, 2 and 5 not guilty of the offences punishable under Section 2(ia)(m), 7(ii), 16(1) ..5..
(a)(i), 2(ix)(k) of the PFA Act and accordingly they were acquitted.
Since the 4th accused was the manufacturer, the trial court maintained conviction against the nominee who is the 3rd accused.

The 3rd accused was convicted and sentenced for the offences punishable under Section 2(ia)
(m), 7(i) and 16(1)(a)(i) and 2(ix)(k) of the PFA Act.

The 3rd accused was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for six months and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- for the commission of offences punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the PFA Act in default to undergo simple imprisonment for two months more.

Further the 3rd accused was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for three months and to pay a fine of Rs.500/- for the commission of the offence under Section 16(1) of the PFA Act and in default to undergo simple imprisonment for one more month.

In appeal, the appellate court by its judgment dated 09.11.2004 allowed the appeal in part and found the 3rd accused not guilty for the offence punishable under Section 2(ia)(m), 7(i) and 16(1)(a)(i) of the PFA Act and accordingly he was acquitted thereunder.

However, he was found guilty for the offence punishable under Section 2(ix)
(k), 7(ii) and 16(1) of the PFA Act and he was convicted and sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for three months and to pay a fine of Rs.500/- and in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for one more month.

10. Heard both sides.
11.
The prosecution was initiated based on Form-III report received from the Public Analyst.
Form-II report also confirmed the finding contained in the Form-III report.
However, it is stated that the food item purchased was misbranded as well.

In Pepsico India Holdings ..7..
Pvt.Ltd. v. Food Inspector and another (2010 (4) KHC 767), the Apex Court held that the laboratories where sample of articles of food for adulteration may be analysed by the Public Analyst in accordance with Section 23(1A) (ee) and 23(1A)(hh) of the PFA Act, 1954.

entities.text:
Pepsico India Holdings ..7..
Pvt.Ltd. v. Food Inspector and another (2010 (4) KHC 767)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Form- III report in this case was not obtained in accordance with Section 23(1A)(ee) and 23(1A)(hh) of the PFA Act.

Hence the lodging of the complaint before the trial court itself was based on an erroneous report of the public analyst and the trial court went wrong in taking cognizance of the offences against the accused.
Hence the conviction and sentence imposed against the revision petitioner/3rd accused is manifestly illegal and is liable to be set aside.
12. The conviction and sentence imposed by the trial court and modified by the appellate court stand set aside.

The revision petitioner/3rd accused is found not guilty of the offences ennumerated hereinabove and ..8..

If any fine amount is deposited during the pendency of the proceedings the same shall be released to the revision petitioner in accordance with law.

In the result, the criminal revision petition is allowed.
